issues.explanation: Three fields (token, e-mail, password) are validated inline, while the project convention reserves inline $request->validate() for one or two fields and asks for a Form Request once rules grow or are shared (the password rule is shared with Register).

Persisting RedirectIfAuthenticated registers this guest-only middleware for every Livewire update request, so as soon as an authenticated Livewire component exists its actions will bounce logged-in users to home; the guest guard should be scoped to the auth components instead.

The suite never asserts that an authenticated user calling submit through /livewire/update is denied, which the project's Livewire policy requires as an unauthorized-call test for each action; only the HTTP GET redirect and the middleware registry entry are checked.

Register puts the e-mail/password rules in a protected rules() method while Login and the rest of app/Livewire use #[Validate] attributes; both work, but mixing the two patterns across sibling auth components is inconsistent.
Switching the provider list to imported short class names is an unrelated refactor that does not help the authentication task.
Removing an unused import and the trailing-newline/quote-style churn in the pt-BR language files are unrelated cleanups that add diff noise.

review.summary: The change implements the complete session-auth flow without a starter kit: Livewire login/register, logout, forgot/reset password, signed e-mail verification, a verified /home, pt-BR-first localisation and a broad Pest suite. Security and task coverage are strong; the deductions are a few convention deviations (three-field inline validation, globally persisted guest middleware), a missing Livewire-level unauthorized-call test, and some unrelated import/whitespace churn, so it is approvable with nits.
